analysis.company_profile: Picnic is a Dutch online grocery retailer that operates a highly automated, low‑cost delivery model, using data‑driven algorithms for demand forecasting, inventory management, routing and personalized shopping experiences.

candidate_positioning: A senior AI/ML engineer with strong production MLOps, time‑series forecasting, and LLM‑driven retrieval expertise who can quickly translate Picnic’s logistics and demand‑forecasting challenges into scalable, observable ML solutions.

team_needs.need: Accurate demand forecasting for inventory and supply‑chain planning
team_needs.evidence: Data Scientist @ Viavi: applied Holt‑Winters and Isolation Forest for demand forecasting across 500+ telecom devices; built SLA breach prediction with LightGBM and FastAPI.
team_needs.gap: Domain shift from telecom to grocery retail and need for large‑scale, SKU‑level forecasting.

team_needs.evidence: Senior AI Engineer @ Optum: built LangGraph‑based analytics and cross‑encoder re‑ranking for dense retrieval; RAG Project Discovery Assistant with semantic retrieval.
team_needs.gap: No explicit experience with collaborative‑filtering or classic recommendation pipelines; focus has been on LLM‑centric retrieval rather than retail recommendation.

team_needs.evidence: Senior AI Engineer @ Optum: engineered LangGraph multi‑agent system for real‑time chart generation and analytics; built automated evaluation pipelines for AI agents.
team_needs.gap: Lacks direct experience with combinatorial optimization or reinforcement‑learning based routing algorithms.

team_needs.need: Robust MLOps, monitoring and observability for production ML services
team_needs.evidence: Multiple roles: MLflow, Docker, Kubernetes, Jenkins, Airflow, automated evaluation & tracing pipelines; built CI/CD for FastAPI services.

team_needs.need: Scalable data pipelines on Spark/Databricks for large SKU and transaction data
team_needs.evidence: Data Engineer @ Nippon: built PySpark pipelines, Databricks workloads; real‑time Elasticsearch observability.

project.name: Dynamic Grocery Demand Forecasting & Adaptive Inventory System
project.problem: Picnic needs SKU‑level demand forecasts that adapt to real‑time sales signals and external factors (weather, promotions) to minimize stock‑outs and waste.
project.approach: Combine classical time‑series (Holt‑Winters, Prophet) with gradient‑boosted models (LightGBM) for SKU‑level forecasts; use a cross‑encoder re‑ranker trained on recent sales to adjust predictions; orchestrate data ingestion and feature engineering with PySpark on Databricks; serve models via FastAPI behind Docker/Kubernetes; track experiments and model drift with MLflow; add LLM‑generated explanations for forecast confidence using Claude/ChatGPT; implement automated monitoring dashboards in Kibana/Power BI.

requirements_not_covered: Direct experience in retail/grocery demand forecasting at SKU level
Built collaborative‑filtering or large‑scale recommendation systems
Reinforcement‑learning or combinatorial optimization for delivery routing
Hands‑on production work with AWS (if AWS is a primary cloud in Picnic’s stack)
